August 6, 2025  
Fabiana Binte Mesbah  
In 2025’s digital landscape, Instagram has become a visual playground where virality meets emotion, where a single photo can spark global conversation within moments. The most liked Instagram post ever tells a lot more than just a story—it reflects shifting cultural moments, powerful fan bases, and the strength of social media marketing. Let’s dive into the top contenders for the most liked posts on Instagram (as of 2025), and explore the stories, strategies, and social signals behind them.  
**Number of Likes:** 75 million  
**Context:**  
Messi’s iconic celebration photo after Argentina's World Cup victory held the crown for quite some time — and for good reason. It combined a historic sports moment with a deeply emotional narrative, uniting football fans and casual users alike in celebration.  
**Takeaways:**  
Posts that capture real, raw human emotion, especially during historic or highly anticipated events, tend to resonate the most. For brands, tapping into emotional storytelling can significantly boost engagement.  
**Number of Likes:** 54.1 million  
**Context:**  
After the epic 2022 World Cup win, Messi shared a carousel of him cradling the trophy like a baby which was an emotional, intimate look at a dream fulfilled.  
**Takeaways:**
**Takeaways:**  
Emotion makes any social media post timeless. Fans love seeing larger-than-life figures in vulnerable, human moments. Personal, candid content drives high engagement and authentic connections.  
**Number of Likes:** 41.5 million  
**Context:**  
Another post from the World Cup celebration, this one featured Messi holding the trophy mid-flight. It radiated triumph and joy.  
**Takeaways:**  
Following up a major event with more behind-the-scenes moments keeps the momentum going — and the likes piling up. Businesses can use this tactic during new launches to create a social media hype.  
**Number of Likes:** 60.9 million  
**Context:**  
In 2019, an unassuming egg photo went viral. The post was fueled by community-powered virality, no brand, no celebrity, and no context.  
**Takeaways:**  
The egg proved that community engagement trumps content sometimes. With a compelling narrative or collective mission, even the simplest visuals can outperform celebrity-driven content.  
**Number of Likes:** 41.8 million  
**Context:**  
Two football GOATs, one frame, and a luxury brand? Instant engagement. This post wasn't just another campaign — it symbolized sportsmanship, legacy, and elite branding, making it one of the most liked posts on Instagram.  
**Takeaways:**  
Collaborations fuel reach. Strategic partnerships of your brand with relevant others enables your post to appeal to a broader audience, leveraging social proof and word-of-mouth (WoM) marketing.
**Number of Likes:** 17.8 million  
**Context:**  
The first photo of baby Stormi shared by Kylie Jenner broke records with just a picture of a mother holding her daughter’s tiny hand. Simplicity and emotional pull – a massive glocal ripple.  
**Takeaways:**  
Intimate and understated posts can have a powerful impact when they reveal something fans deeply care about.  
**Number of Likes:** 26.2 million  
**Context:**  
Fans love real-life relationships, especially when they involve two beloved stars. Zendaya’s heartfelt birthday post for Tom Holland was casual and sweet, hitting all the right notes for her audience.  
**Takeaways:**  
Genuine connection builds loyalty, and drives likes, shares, and saves. Whether it’s between partners, teammates, or collaborators, showing real appreciation humanizes public figures — and boosts engagement.

[confirmed](https://m.entertain.naver.com/home/article/214/0001426266)Monday that the K-pop star’s[Feb. 23 Instagram post](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGZ_zjgSpMP/)had surpassed 16.4 million likes, overtaking Billie Eilish and Cristiano Ronaldo to claim the top global spot for 2025. results.name: What Is the Most Liked Instagram Post of All Time? | WolfPack
results.content:
Last updated on June 23rd, 2026 at 01:41 pm  
Instagram isn’t just a photo-sharing app anymore—it’s a cultural barometer. The posts that rack up millions (or tens of millions) of likes often reflect what people care about, laugh at, or feel deeply connected to. But what does it take to earn the title of the most liked Instagram post? You might be surprised by what tops the list—and what doesn’t.  
In this post, we’ll break down the five most-liked Instagram posts of all time, as of 2025, explore why each went viral, and help you uncover what brands and creators can learn from them.
## 1. Lionel Messi’s World Cup Victory (75M+ likes)  
The most liked Instagram post of all time belongs to Lionel Messi. Shared in December 2022, his post celebrated Argentina’s World Cup victory and featured a carousel of emotional, high-quality images—him holding the trophy, embracing teammates, and smiling with fans. It was more than a sports update; it was a historic and heartfelt moment that fans around the world had waited years to see.  
What made this post so successful was the timing and emotion behind it. It went live just hours after the final match, while fans were still buzzing with adrenaline. Even those who weren’t die-hard soccer fans were drawn to the human side of the story—persistence, triumph, and legacy. From a marketing perspective, the takeaway is simple: Emotional milestones connect. Whether you’re launching a product or celebrating a business win, capturing the moment authentically and posting at the right time can dramatically boost your reach and engagement.
## 2. The Instagram Egg (55M+ likes)  
Sometimes, the internet just wants to have fun. That’s exactly what happened in 2019 when a stock photo of a plain brown egg—yes, an egg—became a global sensation. Posted by the @world\_record\_egg account, the image set out with one simple goal: to beat Kylie Jenner’s most liked post. No filters, no fame, no brand partnerships. Just an egg and a challenge.  
And it worked. In a matter of days, the egg became the most liked Instagram post on the platform. Why? Because it was unexpected, funny, and strangely satisfying. People joined in for the joke, the mission, and the sense of community. Later, the account used its popularity to promote mental health awareness, giving the whole stunt even more meaning. For brands, this shows the power of simplicity and community engagement. You don’t always need polish or celebrity status—sometimes you just need an idea that brings people together.

Before Messi, the viral crown belonged to the World Record Egg in 2019 with 60.6 million likes, a simple picture that proved the internet’s love for quirky trends. Over the years, we’ve seen football legends, pop stars, and even everyday creators dominate the platform.

## **Which is the Most Liked Post on Instagram of all time?**  
**Lionel Messi’s World Cup victory celebration holds the record as the most liked Instagram post of all time**, **with over 74.7 million likes**. Posted on December 18, 2022, the carousel of images showing Messi lifting the FIFA World Cup trophy after Argentina’s historic win became an instant phenomenon, reaching 10 million likes within just 39 minutes.  
This monumental achievement didn’t just break Instagram records—it became the most liked social media post ever across all platforms, surpassing YouTube’s “Despacito” music video and TikTok’s viral content

Several posts have hit 1 million likes in under 10 minutes, with celebrities like BTS and Lionel Messi holding some of the fastest records.
